reviews.Author: Travis h
reviews.OriginDescription: Reviewed in the United States on August 1, 2026
reviews.Text: I bought the Maldon Sea Salt Flakes specifically to refill my salt grinder, and they work really well for that. The flakes aren’t as hard as those little salt pebbles I usually love, which means they dissolve into food faster—perfect when you want the seasoning to melt right in instead of sitting on top. Would be an excellent addition to the top of some homemade chocolate. The only real letdown was the size. I was surprised at how small the box is and how little salt you actually get. My brain clearly didn’t process what 250 grams looks like in practice. Once I realized I couldn’t return it, I just started using it, and I’m glad I did. It makes everything look and taste a bit fancier. Overall it’s a solid product if you like that classic flaky texture and want something that performs nicely in a grinder or as a finishing salt. Just know that with daily use the box won’t last long. Still happy with the purchase.
reviews.Title: 4/5 – Great for grinding and finishing, just wish the box was bigger

reviews.Text: Maldon is a great finishing salt. The flakes have that light, crisp texture that works really well on steaks, eggs, roasted vegetables, and even desserts. It’s an excellent product, but it feels extremely overpriced compared to Costco, especially if you go through finishing salt regularly like I do. The quality is definitely there, so I can still give it 4 stars for the product itself, but the value is harder to justify at this listing price.

I’ve been fortunate that no moisture seems to have contaminated my open package so far. If anyone has a suggestion on where to put the salt after opening this package, please do let me know. Since this was my first time buying this product, I believe I bought the smallest size possible. The taste is quite good and seasons my food to a salty point but not too salty. The texture of the crystals can be seen like small flakes of snow but the feel of the texture when eating also has an inviting crunchiness.

reviews.Text: The salt is as described. Nice and flaky. It provides a nice crunch to foods and of course tastes like salt. The packaging is not great. It comes in a plastic bag inside of a box. I used a quart mason jar which is just the right size for the amount of salt. The seller responded to other reviews that you can put it in a salt cellar etc. which of course you can if you purchase one. It would be better to sell this in a plastic jar rather than a box since that would eliminate the requirement to have some other sort of container to put the salt in. Most other spices come in a plastic container and it can’t be much cheaper, if at all, to use the box and plastic bag used with this. Overall a good product but not the best choice for packaging.

reviews.OriginDescription: Reviewed in the United States on May 24, 2024
reviews.Text: I am a salt fanatic and if you are not you probably won't have the slighted interest in why I think Maldon is one of the best salts available. I love the crystalline crunchiness and the way there are always a few flakes that refuse to melt and hang on to the food as a little surprise. It has a remarkably clean taste; hard to explain but so many salts have an almost ammonia- or bleach-like flavor. I am convinced it makes food taste better than other salts do and if that's my delusion please just leave me to it. It's also pretty. Yup, pleasing to the eye. It twinkles. And it bears the official coat of arms of the royal family of Britain, which tickles me immensely. I ask a lot of my salt and Maldon delivers.

So for presentation (quick, it melts), it might be cool, but really, you can't tell the diff. It's in your mind. Confirmation Bias. You see what you want to see. And especially at the price, are you kidding? So not worth it... but if it were the same price as my Redmond's salt, sure, I'd buy it. But ....just not worth it unless you're really scraping the bottom of the barrel to impress dinner guests -- and again, you'd have to alert them to the nifty salt - and wouldn't that make you kind of weird?

reviews.Text: Fantastic flavor. Nice, big, white salt crystals. Nice as a finishing salt and is particularly fantastic on fresh tomatoes. reviews.OriginDescription: Reviewed in the United States on April 3, 2014
reviews.Text: I ordered this because Martha Stewart spoke so highly of it. I am reviewing it, not from its mineral component, but from it's application to my food. My favorite, most practical form of natural salt is Pink Himalayan salt. I think it is called a "finishing salt." The Maldon Flaked Sea Salt would be useful applying it to the tops of homemade rolls before baking them. It holds up as well as Kosher salt but is smaller, flatter size. I like that about it. I don't anticipate ever running out of this 8.5 oz. purchase. Martha and I don't always agree, I guess.
